name: When should I repair trim instead of replacing it?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair trim instead of replacing it?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repairing trim is often suitable for minor to moderate damage, such as small cracks, chips, or areas of superficial rot. It's a cost-effective option when the underlying structure is sound. Replacement becomes necessary if the trim is severely deteriorated, extensively rotted, or has significant structural damage that compromises its integrity. A professional assessment can determine if repair is sufficient to restore appearance and function or if full replacement is the more durable long-term solution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair trim for minor damage like small cracks or chips, or superficial rot. Replace trim if it's severely rotted, extensively damaged, or structurally compromised.
